messages:
sam: Heads-up — ran into a weird outage case this morning where a control-plane operator restart caused tenants to lose warmup credit accounting and then all their burst requests got rejected. Filing a quick sync to discuss guardrails.

maria: ugh. do we know if it was an ordering/leader election spike or state not persisted?

ajay: saw the incident too. looks like operator reconnected and re-registered pools without the in-memory credit ledger, so allocations fell back to 0. logs attached in the incident thread.

sam: yeah, operator restarted -> re-registered pool -> control-plane assumed fresh state. we rely on operator-local soft-reserve tokens for admission; if those disappear we can't honor prewarm credits.

jen: quick q: are warmup credits only kept in operator memory? i thought we flushed to the control-plane DB periodically.

achris: currently we persist high-water marks but not the ephemeral token counters. design tradeoff was low-latency admission checks without RPCs on every request.

maria: that makes sense for perf but means operator restart window loses tokens. we should decide: restore persisted counters on reconnect, or make reconciliation flow that re-creates tokens from committed reservations.

ajay: proposal: add a simple epoch+replay handshake. operator writes epoch to DB on startup and the control-plane compares. if epoch changed, control-plane replays recent reservation deltas (from compacted WAL) to rebuild token balance before accepting new requests.

sam: I like epoch idea. questions: WAL size and cost, replay latency on large clusters, and correctness if operator crashed mid-write.

jen: alternative: convert token admission to a cheap single-key increment RPC (atomic counter) in the control plane. cheaper to reason about but adds 1 RPC per admit — could be batched.

achris: batching would mitigate RPC overhead but increases complexity. also we'd shift perf hit to control-plane which we want to avoid for latency-sensitive tenants.

maria: tradeoffs summary from me: 1) keep operator-local counters + WAL+replay = low steady-state latency, more complex recovery; 2) central counter RPC = simpler correctness, higher steady-state latency; 3) hybrid: local fast path + occasional sync to central counter with fallback to central RPC when operator state stale.

sam: hybrid sounds pragmatic. implement epoch/WAL small window for quick rebuild, and central RPC fallback when rebuild fails or is stale. ops-bot can flag operator restarts that cause >5s replay time.

ajay: implementation nit: epoch should be monotonic and include operator-id so multiple operator instances can't accidentally claim same epoch. e.g. `{"operator_id":"op-13","epoch":123456}`. store last-acked-epoch in DB.

jen: also add a dead-man switch metric: `operator_reconcile_latency_seconds` and `warmup_replay_duration_seconds`. we can alert on >1s and >5s respectively.

achris: from interface boundary POV, control-plane API needs a new call: `RebuildWarmup(operator_id, epoch, last_commit_ts)` that returns either OK + rebuilt_balance or NEEDS_CENTRAL_RPC. keep it idempotent.

maria: ops runbook change: when operator upgrade is planned, do a coordinated drain: drain admission, snapshot token ledger to DB, then restart. But we still need safety for uncoordinated restarts.

sam: agree. rollout plan: 1) add epoch field and compact WAL, 2) implement RebuildWarmup RPC and central fallback, 3) add metrics/alerts, 4) run canary with 10% of pools, 5) update runbook.

ajay: another corner: split-brain where two ops both think they own pool. epoch+operator_id prevents same epoch reuse, but we should also enforce lease TTL in DB so stale owners can't re-register.

jen: +1 to TTL. add check in registration: if last_heartbeat < now - TTL => reclaim, otherwise reject new owner until lease expires.

maria: one more ops concern: state migration for existing clusters. we need a short DB migration to add epoch column and WAL table. should be zero-downtime but add migration plan.

sam: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and the small schema change. can someone volunteer to prototype the RebuildWarmup endpoint?

ajay: I can take the prototype. will mock WAL replay with compacted deltas first.

achris: I'll own the metrics + runbook edits. jen can you help with migration plan?

jen: yep, I'll write migration steps and the DB migration SQL.

sam: thanks all. leaving the thread with the action items: Sam -> draft RFC follow-up, Ajay -> prototype rebuild endpoint, Chris -> metrics + alerts, Jen -> migration plan, Maria -> ops runbook update.

ops-bot: Incident linked: INC-2026-0423. Auto-tagged on operator_restart event. :information_source:
